title: Place a Free Fraud Alert on Your Credit File
body_md:
A fraud alert is a notice on your credit file asking businesses to verify your identity before opening new credit in your name. It is free, and unlike a credit freeze it does not need to be lifted before you apply for credit.

1. Contact any one of the three nationwide credit bureaus; that bureau must notify the other two:
   - **Equifax**: 800-685-1111
   - **Experian**: 888-397-3742
   - **TransUnion**: 888-909-8872
2. An initial fraud alert lasts one year and can be renewed when it expires.
3. When you place an alert, you can request a free copy of your credit report from each bureau; review all three for accounts or inquiries you do not recognize.
4. Keep the confirmation each bureau sends.

A fraud alert can be used alongside a credit freeze: the freeze restricts who can access your file, while the alert instructs businesses that do access it to verify identity first. Details are at consumer.ftc.gov/articles/credit-freezes-and-fraud-alerts.
